Yes, the buyer is likely to prevail, so the answer is C. The custom-made shutters were screwed and bracketed into the window frames, so under the fixture test (annexation, adaptation and intent) they became fixtures and passed with the home even though the sales agreement didn't mention them. The deed's covenants concern title and encumbrances rather than removal of fixtures, and repairing the frames doesn't change what was conveyed, so A, B and D are wrong.

CONFIDENCE: 88
